## 8B.3 Research Note: Narendra Modi, 2024
Best reading: **mixed, slightly positive on mobilizing the governing apparatus, but with strong counterevidence that the same machinery was also used for partisan and exclusionary politics**.

### Accepted claims
- **India’s president invited Modi to form a coalition government after the BJP lost its solo majority.**  
  - Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint  
  - Date: 7 Jun 2024  
  - URL: https://theprint.in/india/indias-president-invites-modi-to-head-new-coalition-government-swearing-in-on-sunday/2121711/  
  - Claim-level summary: Modi accepted constitutional coalition rule after the setback, which is direct evidence that he could still assemble and lead a governing bloc rather than losing control of the state.  
  - Question IDs: `8B.3`

- **Modi was sworn in for a third term as head of a restive coalition.**  
  - Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint  
  - Date: 9 Jun 2024  
  - URL: https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-sworn-in-as-prime-minister-for-historic-third-term/2123770/  
  - Claim-level summary: The oath-taking shows a normal constitutional transfer and continued executive control despite a weaker mandate, supporting a limited finding of effective political mobilization.  
  - Question IDs: `8B.3`

- **Modi retained all key cabinet ministers and kept the senior ministries unchanged.**  
  - Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint  
  - Date: 11 Jun 2024  
  - URL: https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-prevails-over-allies-in-cabinet-line-up/2126130/  
  - Claim-level summary: This is evidence that Modi preserved control over the core governing team and did not let coalition bargaining fully dilute his command over the executive apparatus.  
  - Question IDs: `8B.3`

- **The first post-election budget directed billions toward jobs, rural programs, and coalition partners.**  
  - Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint  
  - Date: 23 Jul 2024  
  - URL: https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-spends-billions-on-jobs-key-allies-in-first-budget-after-election/2187546/  
  - Claim-level summary: The budget shows Modi’s government could translate political survival into a concrete spending program and use coalition leverage to move policy, but it also shows heavy patronage and bargaining.  
  - Question IDs: `8B.3`

- **The pre-election budget stayed fiscally restrained and explicitly centered the poor, women, youth, and farmers.**  
  - Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint  
  - Date: 1 Feb 2024  
  - URL: https://theprint.in/india/indias-finance-minister-unveils-budget-with-focus-on-poor-women-youth-and-farmers/1948406/  
  - Claim-level summary: This is evidence that the governing program was being routed through formal budget institutions rather than pure vote-buying, which supports effective state mobilization toward a defined program.  
  - Question IDs: `8B.3`

- **The government appointed experienced officials and economists to the Finance Commission.**  
  - Publisher: Reuters via Investing.com  
  - Date: 30 Jan 2024  
  - URL: https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/indian-government-appoints-members-for-new-finance-panel-3287402  
  - Claim-level summary: This supports a technocratic reading of core economic governance: Modi relied on professional fiscal institutions rather than only on personal loyalists.  
  - Question IDs: `8B.3`

- **Modi appointed Sanjay Malhotra, a career IAS officer, as RBI governor.**  
  - Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint  
  - Date: 9 Dec 2024  
  - URL: https://theprint.in/india/india-names-sanjay-malhotra-to-replace-das-as-central-bank-governor/2394973/  
  - Claim-level summary: This is strong evidence of technocratic staffing in a core economic institution, consistent with effective use of bureaucracy rather than overtly politicized capture.  
  - Question IDs: `8B.3`

- **The government approved AI-assisted grievance redress and service-delivery reengineering.**  
  - Publisher: Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions  
  - Date: 18 Jan 2024  
  - URL: https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1997326&lang=2&reg=48  
  - Claim-level summary: This is direct evidence of administrative modernization and state-capacity building, which supports the view that Modi’s team was mobilizing bureaucracy for implementation.  
  - Question IDs: `8B.3`

- **HRW said Modi’s campaign used hate speech against Muslims and other minorities.**  
  - Publisher: Human Rights Watch  
  - Date: 14 Aug 2024  
  - URL: https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/14/india-hate-speech-fueled-modis-election-campaign  
  - Claim-level summary: This is counterevidence: it shows the party’s mobilization strategy relied heavily on communal polarization, which may be effective politically but is a negative form of mobilizing the ruling network.  
  - Question IDs: `8B.3`

- **The Election Commission ordered Modi’s BJP and Congress to show restraint after divisive campaign speeches.**  
  - Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint  
  - Date: 22 May 2024  
  - URL: https://theprint.in/india/indias-poll-panel-orders-modis-bjp-opposition-congress-to-show-restraint-in-campaign/2096809/  
  - Claim-level summary: This is evidence that Modi’s campaign crossed formal lines and required external correction, weakening any claim that the ruling apparatus was being mobilized in a disciplined or neutral way.  
  - Question IDs: `8B.3`

- **The government-created fact-checking unit for online content about the government was put on hold by the Supreme Court.**  
  - Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint  
  - Date: 21 Mar 2024  
  - URL: https://theprint.in/india/india-top-court-puts-on-hold-unit-for-fact-checking-online-content-about-govt/2009612/  
  - Claim-level summary: This is strong negative evidence for 8B.3 because it shows the state trying to build an information-control instrument for the ruling side rather than cleanly mobilizing bureaucracy in a neutral way.  
  - Question IDs: `8B.3`

- **Reuters Institute reported pressure on press freedom, including raids and regulatory powers that critics said could chill scrutiny.**  
  - Publisher: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism  
  - Date: 17 Jun 2024  
  - URL: https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/india  
  - Claim-level summary: This supports the negative side of the lens by showing the state apparatus being used in ways that pressured independent scrutiny, which is inconsistent with clean, institution-led mobilization.  
  - Question IDs: `8B.3`

- **The government did not renew work permits for foreign correspondents, which Reuters Institute described as part of an alarming trend.**  
  - Publisher: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism  
  - Date: 13 Nov 2024  
  - URL: https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/news/inside-modis-crackdown-foreign-press-india  
  - Claim-level summary: This is further counterevidence that the ruling network used state discretion to narrow scrutiny rather than to support open, effective institutional performance.  
  - Question IDs: `8B.3`

- **The Supreme Court struck down the opaque electoral bonds scheme that had heavily benefited the BJP.**  
  - Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint  
  - Date: 15 Feb 2024  
  - URL: https://theprint.in/india/india-top-court-scraps-opaque-election-funding-system-calls-it-unconstitutional/1967048/  
  - Claim-level summary: This is negative background evidence: it suggests the ruling party’s mobilization machinery depended on opaque political finance, which weakens the case for clean or merit-based use of state and party resources.  
  - Question IDs: `8B.3`

### Search gap
- I found **no strong 2024 evidence of direct military mobilization** relevant to this lens. The usable record is mostly about coalition management, bureaucracy, budget execution, election machinery, and information control. That means the strongest judgment here rests on **state/party/bureaucratic mobilization**, not military command.

### Bottom line
- **Positive side:** Modi remained able to mobilize coalition politics, keep cabinet control, preserve technocratic staffing, and push a sizable fiscal/programmatic agenda.
- **Negative side:** the same period also shows communal campaign mobilization, state-linked information control, and pressure on scrutiny institutions.
